description: HEL-1581 parity corpus. Classifies all 27 registered step kinds. A Scala spec (PipelineStepParitySpec) runs every vector through InProcessPipelineEngine.executeTree and a Jest spec (pipelineStepParity.test.ts) runs the TypeScript evaluator over the same files. Each non-server kind has <kind>.json holding step vectors; pipelines.json holds walk vectors. The compute function, operator and literal lists are NOT repeated here: they are read from ../compute-expression-functions.json.

notes: Values: a plain JSON number is a Double; {"$int": n} is an Int; {"$long": "n"} is a Long; {"$double": "NaN" | "Infinity" | "-Infinity" | "-0.0"} is a non-JSON Double. Values compare by value AND class, in both directions.
Long precision: vectors stay within +/-2^53. A Long beyond 2^53 is not representable in the TypeScript value model; this is a known gap, deliberately left open.
Row order is compared; column order is not (Scala rows are unordered Maps).

groupby, aggregate and pivot emit one row per group in Scala's immutable.HashMap iteration order, which the evaluator reproduces (hash of the key Vector, CHAMP trie order). Keys with a fully equal improved hash (every NaN) keep first-seen order, as in Scala, so that case is exact.
A step config with a wrong-typed key cannot be decoded by the Scala engine either (the repository cannot load the step); both runners report it as an error.

Step vectors expect {rows}, {error: true} or {clientDeclines: <reason>, scalaRows | scalaError: true}. Walk vectors carry a scala block (frames | failsAt + framesWithout | laneError + removed + framesWithout | notRun + framesWithout) and a client block ({stepId: {status, rows?}}).
A source secondary's rows pass through JSON on the Scala side, so they can only hold doubles, strings, booleans and nulls, and every row needs the same keys.

window orderBy (and sort) are sorted with a faithful port of java.util.TimSort, so even a non-transitive mixed text/number order matches the JVM, including the 'Comparison method violates its general contract!' failure, which is a step error.
A parentless step whose rootId has no root frame fails the Scala run (an unresolved lane reference); the client marks that step an error and blocks its dependents.

A map-valued step config (rename's renames) reaches Scala through spray-json, which parses every object into a sorted TreeMap: with four or fewer entries the rename fold runs in String.compareTo (UTF-16 code unit) order, with five or more in immutable.HashMap order. The evaluator reproduces both, so integer-like column names need no special case.

Seq[Double].sum reduces from the first element when the collection has a known size (a Vector: all -0.0 sums to -0.0) and folds from 0.0 for a List. Source frames are Vectors; the frame downstream of aggregate / groupby / pivot is a List and stays one. The walk tracks that (listFrame); step vectors run on Vector frames, and two walk vectors cover the List case.

A numeric timestamp string is read with Java Long.parseLong / BigDecimal semantics, which accept any BMP Unicode decimal digit, in cast, datebucket, the compute date functions and window day frames. The chart's own parseChartInstant is ASCII-only there: a pre-existing gap outside this change, recorded as a follow-up.
